name: JUNO Physics and Detector
notes: Classified as a review article rather than a technical design report: it is a comprehensive published physics-and-detector overview (in Progress in Particle and Nuclear Physics), and no source consulted refers to it as a 'Technical Design Report'.

summary.plain: A detailed 2021 paper describing JUNO's physics goals and the final design of its detector, including the light sensors, energy resolution and calibration systems.
summary.technical: arXiv:2104.02565, 'JUNO Physics and Detector' (submitted 2021-04-06): comprehensive description of JUNO's physics program and final detector design, including 20,000 20-inch PMTs (15,000 MCP-PMTs at 28.9% and 5,000 dynode-PMTs at 28.1% average photon detection efficiency), 25,600 3-inch PMTs, a 35 kt water pool, and an effective energy resolution of 3.02%/√E (MeV) in simulations. CORRECTED 2026-09-18: the prior wording attributed the 28.9% figure to all 20,000 PMTs; the abstract states it only for the 15,000 MCP-PMT subset (28.1% for the other 5,000 dynode-PMTs). Note also that the as-built detector (Chin. Phys. C 50, 043001 (2026)) used 17,596 20-inch PMTs, not the 20,000 this 2021 design paper anticipated -- see detector:juno.
